title: Compostela Pilgrim Badge
author: Unknown pilgrim workshop, Santiago de Compostela
description: A cheap pewter badge sold to pilgrims arriving at the shrine of St James, sewn onto a hat or cloak as proof of the completed journey. Thousands of such badges, mass-produced near major shrines, survive as evidence of the sheer scale of medieval pilgrim traffic across Europe.
location_name: Santiago de Compostela, Kingdom of Galicia

title: Letter of Safe Conduct for a Merchant
author: Chancery of the Duke of Burgundy
description: A salvoconduct issued to an Italian merchant travelling through Burgundian territory, guaranteeing protection from tolls and seizure along the road. Such documents reveal how fragile safety was for travelling merchants and how essential political favour was to long-distance trade.

title: Hanseatic Merchant's Account Book
author: Hinrich Sudermann, Lübeck merchant
material: Paper, iron gall ink, leather binding
description: A ledger recording shipments of furs, wax, and grain between Lübeck, Novgorod, and Bruges. The book itself travelled with the merchant's agents, its pages a physical record of a mobile mercantile career spanning the Baltic and North Sea.

title: University Matriculation Register Entry
author: University of Bologna registrar
description: The enrolment record of a student from Kraków who travelled over 1,200 km to study law. Student migration of this kind built dense networks connecting central European towns to Italian universities and back again.

title: Papal Legate's Travel Diary Fragment
author: Anonymous secretary to a papal legate
description: A fragmentary diary describing the legate's journey from Avignon to Prague to negotiate with the imperial court, noting inns, river crossings, and delays caused by weather and local conflict. It offers a rare first-person account of the physical difficulty of diplomatic travel.

title: Woodcut of the Prague Caroline University Seal
author: Workshop associated with Charles University
description: Commemorates the departure of German-speaking masters and students from Prague following the Kutná Hora decree, a mass academic migration that reshaped the map of Central European learning almost overnight.

title: Expulsion Edict Copy
author: Royal chancery of Castile and Aragón
description: A contemporary copy of the edict ordering the expulsion of Jewish communities from Castile and Aragón, setting in motion one of the largest forced migrations of the late medieval Mediterranean world, with routes leading toward Portugal, North Africa, and the Ottoman lands.

title: Venetian Galley Manifest
author: Office of the Venetian Arsenal
description: A cargo and passenger manifest for a state galley bound for Alexandria, listing merchants, pilgrims bound for Jerusalem, and diplomatic couriers travelling together aboard the same regulated convoy.

title: Portrait Medal of a Byzantine Envoy
author: Workshop attributed to Pisanello
description: Cast to commemorate the visit of a Byzantine delegation to the Council of Ferrara-Florence, seeking Western military aid. The medal captures a rare face-to-face encounter between Latin and Byzantine elites amid the slow collapse of Constantinople's hinterland.

title: Guild Letter Recommending a Travelling Journeyman
author: Weavers' Guild of Ghent
description: A letter of recommendation carried by a journeyman weaver moving between guild towns to complete his training, part of the structured circulation of skilled labour that underpinned craft economies across the Low Countries and the Rhineland.

title: Reliquary Casket from a Returning Crusader
author: Levantine or Cypriot workshop
description: Brought back to Western Europe after the fall of Acre, this casket travelled with a returning knight as both a devotional object and a tangible souvenir of a failed campaign, embodying the entangled routes of war, faith, and retreat.

title: London Alien Subsidy Roll
author: Exchequer clerks of the City of London
description: A tax roll listing resident foreigners in London — Flemish weavers, Italian bankers, Hanseatic merchants — taxed specifically for their alien status. The roll is one of the richest surviving sources for tracing everyday immigrant communities in a late medieval city.
